output:
*Interview with Mademoiselle Lina Ruedi, régleuse, in the dining room. Second interview of the night.*

MATTHEY: Mademoiselle Ruedi, thank you for waiting. Please sit down. Tell me about the dinner.

MLLE RUEDI: There is not much to tell about the dinner, Inspector, except the watches. When the Grand Temple struck nine the master made us all take them out, as he does every year. Mine was exact. I regulated it myself and I know what it does. Dr Vauthier's was two minutes ahead. Monsieur Girard would not take his out of his pocket at all, and the master said so, and Monsieur Girard did not like it. The master told each owner what was wrong with his watch. That is his way.

MATTHEY: And after dinner?

MLLE RUEDI: I went up to the atelier and worked beside the master at his bench, under the long windows. We were on the repeater. He had been on that one four years.

MATTHEY: Tell me what happened while you worked.

MLLE RUEDI: The hall clock downstairs struck ten while we were at the bench. It struck when the regulator showed twelve minutes to ten. The master said what he always says about that clock. I will not repeat it, Inspector, because it is his joke and not mine. Then the temple struck ten, and the regulator agreed with the bell exactly. I remember that because it pleased him.

MATTHEY: Did he say anything else?

MLLE RUEDI: He was himself. He was exact and a little impatient, as he always is with the repeater. Then he sent me downstairs when the regulator showed twenty past ten. He did not give a reason and I did not ask for one. The regulator was running then, and he was well. I went straight down to the kitchen.

MATTHEY: Can you explain the repeater to me? I confess I do not understand how it speaks.

MLLE RUEDI: Gladly. When you press the slide, it strikes the hours first, in low notes. Then for the quarter it gives a doubled note, one for each quarter. Then for each minute past the quarter it gives a high note. So if you listen, you can hear the hour, the quarter and the minutes without looking at any dial. The master wanted it to speak the first minute of the new century exactly. That was the whole purpose of four years.

MATTHEY: Did you see him in the kitchen at any time that afternoon?

MLLE RUEDI: Yes. That afternoon I saw him in the kitchen with Rosa's clock in his hands. He was laughing. I did not ask why. It was not my business to ask.

MATTHEY: Were you in the kitchen for the rest of the evening?

MLLE RUEDI: I stayed in the kitchen with Rosa. Madame's piano began, and I looked at Rosa's clock. It showed two minutes to eleven. When the piano stopped, Rosa's clock showed eleven minutes past eleven. I stayed in the kitchen with Rosa until after the temple struck eleven.

MATTHEY: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add?

MLLE RUEDI: Only that I do not guess, Inspector. I tell you what I looked at and what I heard, and I looked at the clocks because that is my work. If you want what the master felt about his repeater, you must ask someone else. I can tell you what it did.
